name: Hubin and Wulin (Shangcheng)
tagline: Downtown shopping streets right on West Lake
description: Hubin runs along the eastern shore of West Lake, where luxury malls and the Wulin Square department stores back straight onto the lakeside promenade. Streets are dense, well kept and full of restaurants, banks and hotels, with metro lines 1 and 2 crossing underneath. It is the most convenient address in Hangzhou and priced accordingly.
bestFor: Nomads who want to step out of the door onto the West Lake promenade every morning.
pros: West Lake walking and running route right there
Metro interchange and airport bus links
cons: Very expensive rents for small older units
Tourist crowds along the lake all year
Traffic jams around Wulin Square constantly

name: Xihu District (Huanglong and Xueyuan Road)
tagline: University side with tea hills behind the lake
description: West of the lake, Xihu District holds Zhejiang University's campuses, the Huanglong sports and business complex and the road up to the Longjing tea villages. It mixes student canteens and cheap bookshops with quiet villa lanes backing onto forested hills. Good bus links and a strong cafe culture make it a practical working base.
bestFor: Nomads who want tea hills and hiking trails minutes from a desk, plus student prices for food.
pros: Hiking and tea plantation trails start at the edge of the district
Cheap student food and lively cafe scene
Quieter than the lakefront but still central
cons: Hilly streets and patchier metro coverage
Weekend traffic from tea village day trippers
Older campus-area apartments are damp in winter

name: Binjiang
tagline: Riverside tech district across the Qiantang
description: Binjiang sits on the south bank of the Qiantang River and is Hangzhou's tech quarter, home to NetEase, Hikvision and dozens of startups in clean low-rise campuses. Wide riverside parks, new apartment compounds and good coffee shops make it comfortable and orderly. The crowd skews young, well paid and Chinese tech workers.
bestFor: Nomads in software who want new buildings, fast internet and a tech crowd to network with.
pros: Newest apartments and the most reliable internet
Long riverside park for running and cycling
Metro line 1 and 4 back into the centre
cons: Feels corporate and empty at weekends
Rents rising quickly with tech demand
Crossing the river adds time to lakeside trips

name: Gongshu (Grand Canal)
tagline: Old canal wharves and warehouse conversions
description: Gongshu covers the northern city along the Grand Canal, where stone wharves, arched bridges and the Qiaoxi historic block have been restored into museums, teahouses and craft studios. Behind them are ordinary residential compounds at clearly lower prices than the lakeside. Canal boats still run into the centre alongside metro line 5.
bestFor: Nomads wanting character and canal walks without paying West Lake prices.
pros: Cheaper than lakeside for similar space
Restored canal district with teahouses and museums
Canal boat and metro links downtown
cons: Older housing stock in the non-restored blocks
Fewer international restaurants or English services
Industrial patches make some streets unattractive

name: Future Sci-Tech City (Yuhang)
tagline: Alibaba's suburb of new towers and wide roads
description: Future Sci-Tech City, along Wenyi West Road in Yuhang, grew up around Alibaba's campus into a district of brand new high-rise compounds, tidy parks and shopping complexes. Apartments are large, modern and well insulated, and prices per square metre beat the centre. Almost everyone here works in tech or e-commerce.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads who value a big modern apartment and clean air over being downtown.
pros: Large modern flats with excellent fibre
Good value space compared with West Lake
Clean, green and well planned with new malls
cons: 40 minutes or more into the city centre
Little character, nothing older than 15 years
Quiet nightlife, you travel in for evenings out
